_about: One Last Amazing Adventure image rights manifest (Version 3.8, NPS public-domain photography only, verified 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-17; Version 4.4 rights audit 2026-11-23 re-checked every record live and replaced or removed the questionable photographs). One entry per photo slot (63 park banners and 248 destinations) on /one-last-amazing-adventure-preview/. Standard: every published photograph must be a public-domain work created by a National Park Service employee as part of official duties. Evidence for each photograph comes from its NPS NPGallery record or (Version 3.7) from the official nps.gov page that publishes it with an NPS photo credit (17 U.S.C. 105 and the NPS website disclaimer). NPGallery evidence: Constraints Information "Public domain: Full Granting Rights" plus documented NPS authorship in the record itself (an NPS photo credit or an NPS copyright entry; an NPS contact or uploader name alone is not accepted), with no volunteer, partner, courtesy, donated, artist-in-residence or other third-party signal. An NPS URL or an "NPS Photo" label alone was not accepted as proof. No Wikimedia Commons, Flickr, Creative Commons, stock, AI-generated or privately owned photographs are used. Slots marked UNRESOLVED show no photograph; researchGap explains why. Add an entry with this evidence before adding any new image.

images.npgalleryTitle: A view of the Kilauea Crater
images.npgalleryDescription:
Crater Rim Historic District. Views of the crater from behind the Volcano House are framed by ferns and low vegetation. This view of the crater rim is the first that many visitors get of Kilauea. The view is observed from a long walkway running the length of the Volcano House. A stone guard wall that follows the path predates the house, when the site was the location of a volcano observatory and volcanologist's residence. It is one of the most accessible views in the park, and it is also unique because of the lush vegetation and sloping crater wall.
